title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's own foundational write-up (1983-84) of 'surgery' on conformal surfaces, which underlies his gluing and cutting philosophy for Riemann surfaces and dessins. That philosophy is the Teichmüller tower and 'Lego' in Esquisse d'un programme.

(1) End of the proof of Theorem 1 (previous page). A conformal surface with boundary is a space locally modelled on open subsets of the closed upper half-plane H̄⁺. Chart changes are topological open embeddings, boundary to boundary, that are holomorphic in the interior. Lemma 1 shows such a chart change f extends holomorphically across the real axis. The tool is Schwarz reflection: a continuous function on U that is holomorphic in U∩H and real on U∩R is holomorphic. To show the extension is a local biholomorphism at a boundary point x (WLOG x = 0, 'OPS x=0'), expand the germ as a_n z^n + … with n > 0 and a_n ≠ 0. Injectivity, together with the fact that f maps the half-disc into the half-plane, forces n = 1. So the germ is invertible and the charts define a structure of 'bordered Riemann surface'.

(2) Theorem 2 (bracketed, stated without proof). The category of compact conformal surfaces with boundary is equivalent to the category of proper smooth algebraic curves over R. The intended construction is the Schottky–Klein double: a bordered X gives X ∪_∂ X̄, a compact Riemann surface with an antiholomorphic involution, hence a real curve. Conversely, a real curve C gives C(C)/complex conjugation.

(3) Part (b): cutting ('découpage') a conformal surface X along a topological 1-complex K ⊂ X. Grothendieck wonders whether regularity hypotheses such as rectifiability or smoothness are needed.
- Theorem 3: the cut surface X̃, with interior X∖K, carries the sheaf of continuous complex functions that are conformal in the interior. With this sheaf it is a conformal surface with boundary.
- Proof plan: every boundary point x̃ of X̃ needs a neighbourhood homeomorphic to H∩D̊, holomorphic in the interior. Two cases follow, according to whether x̃ lies over a point of K of order ≥ 2 or of order 1 (an endpoint). The next page treats these as Lemma 2 a) and b).
- Case a) is a local Riemann map onto one 'side' (rive) of an arc, extended continuously to the arc.
- Case b), at an endpoint, is the slit-disc case handled by a square root.
- Marginal remark: 'C'est un thm. des fonctions univalentes', i.e. Carathéodory-type boundary correspondence.
errors: Theorem 2 as literally stated is not an equivalence if 'surface conforme' means an oriented Riemann surface with holomorphic morphisms. X and its conjugate X̄ (reversed orientation) are generally non-isomorphic as conformal surfaces but have the same double, hence give the same real curve.

Conversely, a real curve C/R gives C(C)/conj, which is in general a Klein surface. This can be non-orientable: the non-separating ('type II') case, including real curves with empty real locus. The orientable bordered surfaces correspond only to separating ('dividing', type I) real curves, plus the geometrically disconnected ones for empty boundary.

The correct classical statement is: compact Klein surfaces (dianalytic structures) ≃ proper smooth curves over R (Alling–Greenleaf 1971). Otherwise one must restrict to dividing curves and add an orientation datum, i.e. a choice of one half.

Regularity of K (rectifiability or smoothness) is unnecessary for Theorem 3. By the Riemann mapping theorem plus Carathéodory's theorem, any topological Jordan arcs (any finite graph topologically embedded, which is automatically tame on a surface) suffice. Grothendieck's hesitation '(rectifiabilité ou lisse ?)' is over-cautious.
Minor: the neighbourhood U should be of x̃ in ∂X̃, not of x.

ideas.what: Boundary charts of a bordered Riemann surface are holomorphic up to the boundary via Schwarz reflection; the leading-term argument a_n z^n forces n = 1
ideas.modern_name: Schwarz reflection principle; bordered Riemann surfaces

ideas.what: Equivalence between compact bordered conformal surfaces and proper smooth real algebraic curves
ideas.modern_name: Schottky/Klein double; Klein surfaces ≃ real algebraic curves
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to real structures and the action of complex conjugation in the Teichmüller tower context; not this statement as such

ideas.what: Cutting a Riemann surface along a graph K gives a bordered Riemann surface whose structure sheaf is the continuous functions holomorphic off K
ideas.modern_name: Cutting along arcs / boundary correspondence (Carathéodory); surgery of Riemann surfaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Carathéodory (1913) for boundary extension; standard in Abikoff, Strebel, etc.
ideas.where_published: Spirit of 'chirurgie' and Lego in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); not this lemma

deep.surprise_reason: Routine foundational material: Schwarz reflection, the classical double / real-curve correspondence (stated slightly incorrectly), and cutting along arcs via Carathéodory. It is of documentary interest only, showing how Grothendieck set up the analytic foundations of his conformal surgery in 1983-84.
transcription_corrections: 'Tels revient à vérifier' should read 'Cela revient à vérifier'.
'un voisinage ouvert U de x' should read 'un voisinage ouvert U de x̃' (in X̃).
Thm 2 should read: 'Équiv. de la cat. des surfaces conformes compactes à bord avec celle des courbes alg. propres lisses sur R' ('celle', not 'celles').
Margin NB: likely 'À partir d'ici H désigne le demi-plan fermé {z∈C | Im z ≥ 0}', with 'fermé' moved.
Left margin near Thm 3: 'C'est un thm. des fonctions "univalentes" (à bord)', where 'à bord' is crossed out.
